source_read_findings.finding: AgentSight is an eBPF-based observability framework that correlates agent/model activity with process, file, resource and network behavior without requiring target SDK instrumentation.
Its architecture is eBPF programs -> JSON/event streams -> native capture core/runners -> analyzers/materialized view -> SQLite/OTel/output.

Live eBPF-backed record/debug modes are Linux-specific and require elevated privilege such as sudo or CAP_BPF plus CAP_SYS_ADMIN; agent-native session/report paths can operate without eBPF on other systems.
TLS interception observes plaintext at SSL/TLS call boundaries; source documentation explicitly warns captured data can include prompts, responses, paths, headers and network targets.

The analysis chain includes an authorization-header remover and saved-session/offline profiling paths use conservative redaction defaults, but plaintext capture still creates a sensitive-data surface.
The project supports SQLite materialized views and OpenTelemetry GenAI export, which are suitable as derived telemetry sinks but are not intrinsically canonical state.

mechanisms.value: Cross-check child-agent launch/exit and subprocess effects independently of F2 self-report.
Detect system-boundary side effects and compare them against typed effect/journal traces without granting authority.
Provide an independent measurement plane for child cost, retries, latency and process resource usage.
Potential schema/adapter donor for exporting derived telemetry without coupling it to UnifiedDB authority.

hypothesis: A narrowly scoped AgentSight-derived read-only witness can improve F2 telemetry falsifiability by independently observing child processes and selected system effects, especially for WP005/WP605/WP902/WP904, while UnifiedDB and EffectGate/EffectJournal remain the only canonical state/effect authorities.
counterhypotheses: F2-native telemetry may already provide enough information, making eBPF complexity and privilege overhead net-negative.
TLS plaintext capture may create unacceptable secret/privacy exposure relative to its additional information gain.
Kernel/process observations may correlate with effects but still fail to prove F2 causal identity unless joined through explicit session/task/effect IDs.
AgentSight SQLite/OTel views may introduce a stale second-memory temptation unless enforced as disposable derived witness data.
Platform-specific probe behavior and statically linked TLS binaries can create systematic blind spots that look like absence of activity.

cheapest_high_information_next_discrimin.proposal: On an admitted F2 test surface, run the same deterministic child/effect fixture twice: baseline F2-native telemetry only, then F2-native telemetry plus a process/file-only AgentSight witness with TLS payload capture disabled. Join by explicit process/session/time/effect correlation and score incremental detection, false positives, dropped events, CPU/RAM/latency overhead and provenance closure.
cheapest_high_information_next_discrimin.acceptance_signal: AgentSight witness catches at least one intentionally hidden/missing application-level event or materially improves root-cause localization while staying within bounded overhead and producing zero canonical/effect authority writes.
cheapest_high_information_next_discrimin.falsifier: No incremental observability benefit over F2-native telemetry, unacceptable privilege/overhead, non-joinable causal identity, or any requirement for TLS plaintext to obtain the claimed core benefit.
